subject: Renewal: capacity increase + price anchoring request
messages:
From: Alex D'Souza <alex@celestia.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@celestia.ai
Date: 2026-03-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — Q2 capacity uplift and price anchoring

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the QBR last week. Celestia had a strong quarter and we expect production usage to scale faster than our original forecast — primarily around embeddings and reranking. Before we start internal procurement, procurement team asked me to get a concrete renewal proposal from Redwood that does two things:

1) Locks a price (or limited step increases) for 12 months to avoid token-cost volatility while we finalize our architecture.
2) Adds an incremental committed tier of 200k embedding units/month for 6 months (as a trial uplift) with clear true-up terms.

I've attached a small usage summary for January–February to help. High level ask: can Redwood provide a price-anchored renewal with a short-term uplift that doesn't immediately raise our effective unit price? We'd prefer to avoid a multi-month RFP if possible.

If you can share a draft term sheet and any operational guarantees (latency SLO for embeddings, burst capacity headroom), we can loop in procurement this week.

Best,
Alex D'Souza
Head of Product
Celestia Analytics

Attachments: celestia_q1_usage_summary.csv (CSV, 47 KB)

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex D'Souza <alex@celestia.ai>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — Q2 capacity uplift and price anchoring

Alex — thanks for the note and the data, and congrats on the strong quarter.

Quick read: the usage spike is clear and we can support the 200k uplift as a time-limited committed add-on. High-level proposal I can share internally today:

- 12-month renewal with a 6-month trial uplift of +200k embedding units/month.
- For the uplift period: hold current per-embedding rate for the first 3 months, then a single step increase (if needed) capped at +8% for months 4–6.
- True-up at the end of the 6-month uplift vs. actual consumption (standard true-up window).
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile embedding latency < 45 ms on Dedicated pool; Redwood will reserve 1x burst headroom during business hours for the first 3 months.

I'll work with David and Monica to convert this into a short term-sheet and a pricing appendix. Can you confirm the procurement contact and a target signature date? If procurement wants a longer lock we can pivot to a 12-month price hold for committed volumes — that will need an uplift commitment on the overall spend.

Thanks — I'll circulate a draft term sheet by end of day tomorrow.

— Rachel
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Renewals
Redwood Inference

Rachel / Monica — quick ops and pricing notes based on Alex's ask:

- We can provision the 200k embedding uplift on Dedicated as a temporary overlay using an isolated pool. Ops estimates ~24–48 hours to spin up and validate KV cache warming.
- If we offer a 3-month full price hold and then a capped step increase (Rachel's outline), pricing can be modeled two ways: 
  * Option A (preferred for Celestia): Maintain current unit price for uplift for 3 months, then step to a blended price for months 4–6 capped at +8%. No retroactive adjustments other than true-up reporting.
  * Option B: Provide a deeper discount (3–5%) on the uplift volumes in exchange for a 12-month minimum committed spend parity across product lines.
- Risk note: bursts beyond reserved headroom during the trial month will be billed at standard overage rates unless we pre-approve additional temporary capacity. Recommend including a clear overage threshold and a notification cadence.

I'll draft the ops bullet points for the term sheet and a runbook for provisioning/monitoring. Ben — can you run a quick margin check on Option B and share whether that discount is feasible at the requested uplift size?

Thanks,
David
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-05T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — Q2 capacity uplift and price anchoring

Looping in my quick economics take.

- Option A (short hold then capped step): margin-neutral with small operational cost absorbed by burst buffer. Approve as-is.
- Option B (deeper discount for 12-month parity): requires ~3.5% discount across uplift volumes to be competitive; net margin falls by ~1.8 percentage points but could be offset if Celestia signs a full-year commit at 1.25x their current run-rate.

Recommendation: present both options to the customer as a choice. If procurement needs a longer anchor, lead with Option B but require a minimum committed spend and add a mid-term usage review at month 6.

I'll attach a clean pricing appendix for Rachel to include in the draft term-sheet.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Account Manager
Redwood Inference
